PullRequest.Title: Add prompt options to V3 onboarding
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add the `options` variation to the V3 new-session onboarding tour and make it the default
- show four responsive prompt cards populated from actionable GitHub issues/PRs with standard fallbacks
- support cancellable workspace-aware reloads, safe prompt replacement, accessibility, and selected/disabled states
- add full new-session component fixtures and focused unit coverage

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\onboardingTours\test\browser\newSessionViewV3Prompt.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\onboardingTours\test\browser\newSessionViewV3Tour.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\newSessionPromptOptions.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\newChatWidget.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\newSessionComposerService.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\sessionsRename.test.ts`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The default change, awaited call path, query limit, absence of caching, request count, concurrency, and timeout are directly established by the code. Only real-world request duration is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub GraphQL requests and repository-discovery filesystem operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each resolution performs two summary requests, up to one issue-linkage request, and one review-thread request per eligible authored PR up to five; the entire uncached cost repeats per workspace change.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased first-run and workspace-refresh latency plus excessive network traffic
Findings.PreviousBehavior: An absent treatment selected the local prompt path, which performed no repository filesystem discovery or GitHub API calls. The GitHub fan-out was limited to the explicitly assigned githubPrompt variation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: An absent or empty treatment now selects personalized prompt options, which await repository discovery and uncached GitHub issue and pull-request resolution before replacing loading skeletons.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 193 returns `options` for undefined or empty treatments, moving this boundary fan-out from an explicit GitHub variation onto the common no-treatment path.
Findings.Title: Batch GitHub lookups before making options the default
Findings.Impact: Eligible first-time users can see prompt cards remain as loading skeletons until the slowest of up to eight GitHub requests completes, and each draft workspace change repeats the burst, increasing API traffic and rate-limit pressure.
Findings.Evidence: The options resolver awaits issue and PR branches. The issue branch makes a summary request and a linkage request. The PR branch makes a summary request, then `_resolveReviewCandidates` starts one review-thread GraphQL request for every eligible PR with `Promise.all`. The fetcher returns up to five PRs and these service methods are uncached, yielding up to eight requests per resolution and six concurrent requests; final options wait for every request or the six-second outer timeout. Workspace changes call the resolver again.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the options experience but include review-thread data in the existing authored-PR GraphQL query, or otherwise batch and coalesce the per-repository lookup, so candidate ordering is retained without per-PR fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: First eligible user completes the V3 workspace step with no variation treatment and waits for default prompt options
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The sequence run step awaits `refreshPromptOptions`, which awaits repository discovery and all issue/PR candidate lookups before resolved cards replace the skeletons. This blocks option availability and onboarding sequence completion, although the text input itself remains interactive.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search up to 50 parent directories for `.git`, then read `.git`/`commondir`/`config` when repository metadata is unavailable
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 50 sequential stat calls plus a small bounded number of file reads per resolution; usually fewer for shallow local paths
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The no-treatment default used the local prompt path and did not perform repository filesystem discovery; this boundary was reached only by the explicit githubPrompt variation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before GitHub requests can begin, bounded only by the outer six-second option timeout

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the selected repository through the Git service when metadata, URI, and direct config resolution fail
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one openRepository call per resolution
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Not reached by the previous no-treatment local-prompt default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repository identification must complete before cards resolve; it is bypassed when earlier metadata/config checks succeed

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query recent assigned issues, issue linkage, recent authored PRs, and review threads for each eligible PR
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two fixed summary requests, up to one linkage request, and up to five review-thread requests: eight total, with up to six simultaneously after summaries return
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The no-treatment default made zero GitHub calls; equivalent fan-out was limited to users explicitly assigned githubPrompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolved cards wait for both branches and every review request, or for the six-second outer timeout

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The authored-PR search is capped at five, so review request count scales from zero to five eligible non-failing PRs; issue linkage covers up to five issues in one request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Issue and PR branches run concurrently. After summaries, up to five review-thread requests run in parallel while issue linkage can also be active, for effective concurrency up to six.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The recent-work service methods have no result or in-flight cache. Both cold and repeated resolutions issue the same calls; authentication absence is not negatively cached here.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default-selection change, awaited path, fetch limits, request fan-out, and lack of caching are explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual filesystem depth, GitHub latency, and how many eligible users have five authored PRs vary. The six-second timeout and one-time onboarding eligibility bound the worst visible wait, supporting medium rather than high severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff moves a bounded but substantial uncached network fan-out onto the common default path, delaying first prompt-card availability.

Scenarios.Scenario: User changes the draft workspace while prompt options remain mounted
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workspace watcher clears/cancels the old refresh and starts the same resolver for the new repository; the new cards remain loading until repository discovery and candidate requests complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat Git repository discovery for the newly selected workspace
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded parent walk per distinct workspace selection
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Workspace changes did not refresh prompt options or trigger this discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes personalized-card network requests and therefore delays refreshed cards

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat all recent-work and review-thread GraphQL lookups for the new repository
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to eight requests per workspace change, after repository grouping; returning to a previous repository is not cached
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No prompt-option reload or corresponding GitHub requests occurred on draft workspace changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new card set waits for all requests or timeout; input interaction is otherwise off this critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost grows linearly with workspace changes and, within each repository, with up to five eligible authored PRs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The prior token is canceled before refresh; each current refresh can still launch up to six concurrent requests, with brief transport overlap possible while canceled requests unwind.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no warm repository-result cache or in-flight coalescing. Cancellation prevents stale publication but does not make a later visit warm.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new autorun explicitly refreshes on URI changes and the resolver has no cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rapid repeated workspace switching is less common than initial onboarding, and cancellation may stop some in-flight transport work early.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the same reported boundary-fanout issue; no separate duplicate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: User selects, replaces, or edits one of four prompt cards, including responsive rendering
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selection focuses the editor and performs one prompt animation or full-model replacement. Each editor change updates four button states synchronously; resize is handled by CSS container queries.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work is bounded by four cards and one editor model; button-state work is O(4) per edit and DOM rendering creates a fixed number of nodes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A `_selecting` guard serializes option selection. Typing animation is cleared before replacement or refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache or expensive lookup is involved after options have resolved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed widget and input listener show fixed-size iteration and no boundary calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prompt strings vary modestly in length, but cardinality remains fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable synchronous UI, rendering, retention, or cleanup regression; the fixed-size per-keystroke work and four skeleton animations are bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 16 changed files and all diff pages. One medium-confidence-impact/high-mechanism-confidence boundary-fanout regression was submitted: the no-treatment default now awaits uncached repository and GitHub lookups, including up to five parallel per-PR review requests. UI interaction, cancellation ownership, DOM lifecycle, and fixed-size input/render paths did not yield additional findings.
